wa_outer_space_2.notes: The common start is the first three pitches of the neighbouring route Remorse, which keeps the overall grade at 5.9. It begins close to where the approach trail reaches the wall, climbing broken, blocky mid-fifth-class ground to a roomy ledge for the belay.
Climb cracks straight up a short way, then trend left to a thin flake and keep traversing left below it to a ledge belay.

A chimney and blocks lead to the ledge where Outer Space proper begins. The original easier start (5.7, one or two pitches that can be simul-climbed) instead goes up a left-trending corner and scramble and then traverses past a fixed sling to the large ledge with bushes; it is easy to lose the route here.

Start up a hard crack or the dihedral to its left, reach a roof, then step out right on the famous exposed finger traverse and follow the crack right until it heads up again. Protection is good but rope drag builds. Some of the flakes on the lower crack are hollow, and one key flake was thought to have been torn off in 2021, so check holds and gear. Belay on a sloping ledge.

Move left from the belay on an easy slab with knobs, then make exposed face moves to a right-facing dihedral forming the right side of a pedestal. The dihedral is the crux of the pitch. Top out, clip the bolt above, and traverse across to the pedestal's left side, belaying at the base of the splitter. It is longer than it looks and drags on the rope.

The standout pitch: a long splitter hand crack through the shield, with bomber jams and knobs on the face when the arms tire. Doubles or triples in hand sizes help avoid running out of gear. The pitch finishes on an ideal ledge, where a second crack takes the anchor.

A bouldery move leaves the ledge, then the crack continues as easy jamming to the top. Gear goes up to about 3.5 inches. A 70 m rope reaches the summit boulder, which takes small gear, but not the trees 30 ft further. Save small cams or bring the second up before the low-angle chickenhead finish; the last stretch to the top is about 50 ft of scrambling.

wa_south_early_winter_spire_passenger.notes: Approach a massive roof and traverse left beneath it, clipping one bolt, to a bolted belay -- sets a sustained, technical tone for the route.
Pull the roof (a bolt protects the lip) via strange flares and campus moves to the right, into a crack with some vegetation and flared sections.
An outstanding, sustained finger crack runs to a roof/slot intersection -- pure splitter climbing on perfect granite.
The route's crux: move left and down past two bolts, climb a runout section past more bolts to a roof, then pull face moves past a bolt for the hardest moves on the route.
Move up and right to a crack, then step left into a clean 5.10 corner-and-splitter finish.
A sustained thin-hands crack eases into a left-leaning ramp and corner system.
Easier splitters and blocks lead up and left to the South Arete topout, or a revised finish climbs a shallow finger crack straight up from a gear belay.

wa_the_brothers_traverse.notes: From the terraces near 5,500 ft (a possible bivy), head roughly north over ground that is occasionally fourth class, aiming for the notch in the South Brother's southeast ridge at about 6,100 ft.

Pass through the notch into the Great Basin, descend steep snow and contour north to the couloir that leads to just below the North Brother's summit. The route is best in early season (April–May); snow cover changes it drastically, and later in the year the gullies fill with dense brush.
wa_the_brothers_traverse.pitch: Great Basin to the North Brother

wa_the_brothers_traverse.notes: The roped traverse starts below the North Brother: scramble down easy rock to a flat spot to rope up, then belay a pitch of moderate snow on the east side of the ridge, protected with pickets and rock gear.
A second moderate snow pitch continuing south along the east side of the ridge on pickets and rock gear, to the point where the line crosses to the west side.
Cross to the west side of the ridge for a rock traverse with sparse protection.
Another traversing rock pitch leads to a further notch in the ridge.
From the notch go down and west to reach snow and build a belay in a moat.
A mixed rock-and-snow pitch leads to a second moat at the foot of a steep couloir.
Climb the steep couloir. At its top, an easy unroped scramble left leads into the gully beside the South Brother's summit and up to the top.
